question: Your CI pipeline runs Claude Code to review each pull request. The system prompt gives detailed instructions for the review comment format, but the output still varies: some comments omit the file location, and others omit the severity or the suggested fix. Developers say that these inconsistent comments are hard to act on. Which changes would most effectively make the review comments consistent and actionable?

options.text: Rewrite the format section of the system prompt with longer and more detailed rules for each field of a review comment.
options.reason: The guide states that detailed instructions alone produce inconsistent results; the prompt already has detailed instructions, so more of them is not the effective fix.

options.text: Ask Claude to add a self-rated confidence score to each review comment so that developers can skip the unclear ones.
options.reason: The guide notes that self-reported confidence is poorly calibrated, and a score does not make the missing location, severity, or fix appear in the comments.

options.text: Add a sentence to the system prompt that asks Claude to be thorough and consistent in every review comment it writes.
options.reason: The guide says that general instructions of this kind do not reliably change output; concrete examples are needed to show what consistent output looks like.

options.text: Add few-shot examples of complete review comments that each show the location, issue, severity, and suggested fix in the exact desired format.
options.reason: The guide names few-shot examples that demonstrate the desired format (location, issue, severity, suggested fix) as the most effective way to get consistent output when instructions alone fail.

options.text: Make the few-shot examples cover several kinds of findings, such as a security flaw and a style issue, all written in the same format.
options.reason: Targeted few-shot examples across varied findings demonstrate the format concretely and help the model generalize it to new cases, which the guide describes as the strength of few-shot prompting.
